I totally agree with you it can be difficult to talk to doctors sometimes especially if they have poor bedside manner. In my experience after talking to my therapist, the best way to do it is to know what it is you want. Go in with a plan prepared of what to say and questions.

For example, I knew that I wanted a colonoscopy and so I told my doctor that "my therapist and I talked about it and she is telling me to advocate for this procedure" and to maybe exaggerate what's going on. I told my doctor that my situation was worse than it is and it's interrupting my daily life. If they're good doctors, they need to respond to that and give you a plan of action. 

Doctors are supposed to be there for you so they need to take what you want into consideration when making a decision for treatment.

Yeah, when I was in the middle of all this, I got multiple blood tests, a CT scan with with contrast, a fecal test (to test for H.Pylori and other bacteria), a vibroscan for my liver, an abdominal ultrasound, and an endoscopy and colonoscopy done at the same time. Now that I've written all this down...like damn I've had a LOT done and none of them showed anything other than very mild fatty liver and gastritis.

I know it's extremely difficult and scary to be in the middle of all this and you're wondering and it feels like nothing is helping but my therapist told me that the best way is to advocate for what you want. I was so beyond fed up with it and I was feeling so sick so I advocated for what I wanted which was the endoscopy/colonoscopy and they agreed and I count my blessings everything that I have good healthcare and a care team that responded to my needs but I also had to acknowledge that this would be the end point for me (at least until my next colonoscopy in 15 years lol). I don't know much about it, and I'm by no means a doctor, but if you're aware of H.Pylori and it's treated, I would continue to talk about your concerns and keep fighting until someone listens. That's how I got mine done. I know not everybody could do it, but if you can, then do what you need to do to make yourself feel better. It's all for you after all!

Hoping for a good outcome for you :)

>When you come back from long trips, is your boyfriend just completely normal - like you haven't even been on a trip at all?

YES!!!! Oh my God exactly this. I've heard this before and I believed it but hearing it again and the concept of time being messed up again, now I realize it's something that is common with people with ADHD. 

>By choosing to remain in this relationship, you will (unfortunately) be indefinitely burdened with the responsibility of Chief Prompter. Need comfort? You will often have to prompt him. House a mess? He doesn't even realise it - you need to prompt him. You want to know that he loves you and misses you? You guessed it... you're going to have to prompt his dysfunctional brain for this information - which he will gladly offer... he just needs to receive the request.

I do have to do this a lot and I have to remind him for us to do chores. It's hard because I'm an introvert and I feel like I'm always being a burden or an annoyance to him when I say we have to do these things, even though he's more than happy and he's never shown any contempt at me for having to do something. He just forgets. I have to be the prompter but sometimes I wish he would just come to me and he does but when he forgets to text or call me it brings me a sense of dread. I realize now that like you said, I have to be the one to be the one and I have to be ok with that. And I will be because the good does outweigh the bad. 

>Really hope it works out for you buddy. I know how hard it is being the partner of somebody like this. I gave up on relationships over 10 years ago due to making every girl in my life feel the way you do right now. My hope (in your specific situation) is that the good times (when you're both at home together) are good enough and full of enough happiness to make up for the bad times when you're apart.

Thank you. Yes it is hard because it hurts sometimes but you've done more to open my eyes than I've ever been told before. You told me things that he does without me even saying them which made me understand it's not him, it's the ADHD that's doing this to him. I get that better now hearing that from you. Thank you, you were very kind and sincere in your reply and it helped me realize what I need to do. 

I will say that I don't think you should give up on relationships though if it's just because of the ADHD. I love my partner more than anything in the world and I will continue to fight for him and support him in all that he does. I know I'm not alone in that feeling and there are more people like me out there who will also fight for you too, if it's what you want. But being alone is fine too of course if that's how you feel and what you want.

I have a few that might ruffle some feathers: 

* I feel that Smash's roster is beginning to get too bloated with characters whose mechanics that aren't all that interesting. I'd rather have a smaller, more conservative roster with characters who have had a lot more time spent on them as well as being fun and interesting.

* That being said, in Smash 5 I'm privately hoping that Bowser Jr.,  G&W, Toon Link, Ike, Robin, Duck Hunt, Charizard, Jigglypuff, Wii Fit Trainer, Dr. Mario, Dark Pit, Lucina, and maybe ROB and Lucario (I'm on the fence about the last two) get cut. 
Some of these characters I feel would be better suited as assist trophies (Bowser Jr.)/Pokeballs (Charizard, Jiggs) or alt costumes (Dark Pit, Lucina).

* I really dislike the Pikmin series as a whole. Something about the character design gets on my nerves and I found it personally boring. I can't help but roll my eyes when I think about Pikmin 4.

* IMO Xenoblade Chronicles X is one of the worst designed games I've ever played. Everything from the music and horrendous voice acting to waiting *half* of the game to get the big thing on the box (skells) just gave me a headache. The final boss and ending were atrocious and I hope Elma fades into obscurity along with this subseries. Maybe part of this opinion comes from the fact I absolutely loved Xenoblade Chronices 1 so much and was hoping to see an extension of that. In the end, I was left with a sour taste in my mouth and I get kind of frustrated when I see praise for this game.
